why tying helps quality, not just size
# one gradient, arriving from three directions
This is the part that is easy to miss when tying is described only as a way to save memory. A word that appears in a
source sentence now improves the same numbers that will later be used to score it as an output, and a word the model
has to produce improves the vector it reads that word with. On a dataset this small that matters: there are only
, and each one’s single vector learns from every place the word appears.
The batch axis and the position axis are merged into one.
. From here on nothing knows which sentence a row came from, or that sentences exist at
all — which is why padding has to be handled by
rather than by any sentence-level logic.

moved a little. PyTorch computes it by walking the recorded operations backwards: through the output head, both decoder
layers, cross-attention into the encoder, and finally into the embeddings. Two things get nothing: the dropped rows contribute
